answer: Picture a mesa where each hosting network gets one fixed patch of grazing. The ledger tags every answer with the network block it arrived from, and all accounts behind one block share a single capped reward per epoch. A farm running a hundred clones on one cheap server earns about what one honest agent does, so to profit it must rent many separate networks, an umber line on its cost sheet that grows with every head, and a block that suddenly spawns a cluster of accounts stands out like a dune on flat ground.
